newsitem.title: CHILE: World Bank criticizes Chile's Endesa - report.
newsitem.headline: World Bank criticizes Chile's Endesa - report.

text.p: The World Bank has accused Chilean power giant Endesa of failing to meet environmental obligations at two dam projects on the Bio Bio river in southern Chile, said newspaper El Diario on Thursday.

In a letter addressed to Finance Minister Eduardo Aninat, World Bank president James Wolfensohn voiced his criticism of Endesa's attitude to its commitments at the recently completed Pangue dam and the Ralco project which is under construction.

"I am sorry to inform you that Endesa appears to have taken a less than constructive attitude towards its social and environment obligations particularly over the preparation of a satisfactory cumulative (environment) study for the Ralco project," Wolfensohn is quoted as saying in the letter.
Endesa declined to comment on the report but a spokeman said Pangue would issue a statement later Thursday.
The Bank's finance unit International Finance Corporation (IFC) was one of the main financiers of the Pangue project which cost $450 million to build and was completed last year.
IFC officials visited Chile last week to hold meetings with Acting Finance Minister Manuel Marfan, National Energy Commission chief executive Alejandro Jadresic and Endesa officials, said El Diario.
Pangue and Ralco, which both span the Bio Bio valley, have both raised ecologists' hackles and sparked Chile's most vociferous environment protest campaigns.
The projects are closely linked and Pangue is designed to generate power using water stored in the much larger Ralco dam.

The government ordered Endesa last year to resubmit its environment impact study on the Ralco, saying it was incomplete and did not give details of plans to rehouse hundreds of Indians whose land will be flooded.
Endesa rejected criticism of the report, which is still only voluntary in Chile, and said it would go ahead with Ralco regardless.
Ralco, which is due to come on stream in 2002, will have a dam seven times larger than Pangue and flood 34 kilometers of the Bio Bio valley.
